concepts.title: Random Experiments and Sample Spaces
concepts.definition: A random experiment produces one of several outcomes that cannot be foretold in advance, and the sample space gathers every possible outcome; the same experiment can carry different sample spaces depending on what the observer chooses to record.
concepts.key_idea: List the sample space once; every event is a subset of it.

concepts.title: Probability of an Event and Its Complement
concepts.definition: For equally likely outcomes, the probability of an event divides the number of favourable outcomes by the total number of outcomes, and the probability of the negated event is one minus that value.
concepts.key_idea: Favourable over total; whatever is missing from the event carries the complement.

concepts.title: Types of Events
concepts.definition: Events get named by how they relate: mutually exclusive events cannot share an outcome, exhaustive events cover the whole sample space together, independent events leave each other's probabilities unchanged, and events of probability zero or one are impossible or sure.
concepts.key_idea: Check the intersection for exclusivity, the union for exhaustiveness, and influence for independence.

concepts.title: Conditional Probability
concepts.definition: Knowing that one event has occurred shrinks the sample space, and the probability of a second event inside that shrunken space equals the count favouring both events over the count favouring the given event.
concepts.key_idea: Rescale within the given event; divide the overlap by the condition.

concepts.title: Independent Events and Combined Occurrence
concepts.definition: When two events do not influence each other, the chance of both occurring multiplies the separate chances; the chance that at least one occurs comes from one minus the chance that neither does.
concepts.key_idea: Independent means multiply; at least one is the complement of none.

solution_steps.explain: independence lets none-occurrence multiply

concepts.title: Theorem of Total Probability
concepts.definition: When disjoint scenario events partition the sample space, the probability of any outcome totals the scenario probabilities weighted by the outcome's conditional chance in each scenario.
concepts.key_idea: Split by scenarios, weight each branch, then add the branches.

concepts.title: Bayes Theorem and Posterior Probability
concepts.definition: Bayes theorem reverses the conditioning: after evidence is observed, each hypothesis is re-weighed by multiplying its prior probability with the likelihood of the evidence, divided by the overall probability of the evidence.
concepts.key_idea: Prior times likelihood over total evidence turns a prior into a posterior.
